 Health care, housing, wages: Josh Turek outlines campaign goals at Davenport rally 
 Iowa Senate candidate Josh Turek made a stop in the Quad Cities Thursday, meeting with voters at Modern Woodmen Park. By Elisabeth Ruggiero and KWQC Staff Published : Oct. 22, 2026 at 9:41 PM CDT Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google DAVENPORT, Iowa (KWQC) - Iowa Senate candidate Josh Turek made a stop in the Quad Cities Thursday, meeting with voters at Modern Woodmen Park.
 Turek touched on the reasons he’s running for Senate, to raise the minimum wage, realign Iowa’s education system to keep up with the rest of the nation and bring back funding for healthcare.
 “I’m gonna fight for a livable wage because $7.25 is not a livable wage for families,” Turek said. “Second, I’m gonna go up there and fight to drive private equity outta housing and health care and nursing homes. I’m gonna fight for affordable and accessible health care because I’m someone that believes that health care is a human right and you shouldn’t have to win the genetic lottery to have access to basic health care.”
 Republican candidate, Rep. Ashley Hinson spoke at President Donald Trump’s rally in Sioux City .
 Iowa 1st Congressional District candidate Christina Bohannan was also at Turek’s rally Thursday evening. Her opponent, Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks held a manufacturing roundtable in Burlington, Iowa, earlier in the day.
